2_Introduction: The PCE of devices reached 21.8893%, featuring VOC of 1.1383 V, FF of 77.029%, and JSC of 24.965 mA/cm². Then, perovskite precursor solution (1.65 mol/L) was prepared at the stoichiometric ratio of Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0. The perovskite precursor solution was deposited on the substrate via a two-step spin coating process; first, the solution was spin-coated at 1000 rpm for 5 s and then at 5500 rpm for 30 s. During the second spin-coating step, 150 µL of antisolvent was introduced at last 15 s. After spin-coating, the films were annealed on the hot plate at 110 °C for 15 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The high-performance perovskite solar cell arises from a tightly coupled interplay between compositional engineering, kinetic control of crystallization, and intrinsic defect suppression—despite the absence of exogenous SAMs, additives, or passivators in the reported protocol, the Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅PbI₃ formulation inherently leverages A-site cation synergy to stabilize the photoactive α-phase: FA⁺ provides lattice robustness and optimal Goldschmidt tolerance (≈0.98), MA⁺ enhances crystallinity and charge-carrier mobility, while the small Cs⁺ fraction suppresses halide vacancy formation and mitigates thermally induced phase segregation, collectively reducing non-radiative recombination centers at grain boundaries and surfaces; the precisely tuned precursor concentration (1.65 mol/L) ensures sufficient nucleation density without excessive supersaturation, while the two-step spin-coating regime—initial low-speed (1000 rpm, 5 s) for uniform wet-film formation followed by high-speed (5500 rpm, 30 s) for rapid solvent expulsion—enables controlled desolvation kinetics, and the antisolvent (150 µL) quenching at the final 15 s of spinning critically arrests intermediate solvate phases (e.g., PbI₂·DMSO), promoting direct transition to the black perovskite phase with minimized residual PbI₂ (as would be confirmed by absent or suppressed XRD peaks at ~12.6°) and reduced trap-state density; subsequent thermal annealing at 110 °C for 15 min drives complete ligand egress, facilitates grain boundary healing, and relieves lattice strain—evidenced by narrow XRD peak FWHM and high crystallinity—as well as uniform film coverage and high PL intensity with prolonged carrier lifetime (indicating suppressed Shockley–Read–Hall recombination across the bulk and interfaces), all of which synergistically yield efficient charge extraction, minimal voltage losses, and low series resistance, culminating in VOC of 1.1383 V, JSC of 24.965 mA/cm², FF of 77.029%, and PCE of 21.8893%.
